﻿COS_Architecture_gov_dft
Draft governance baseline — version 0.1.0
Created 20-Oct-2026 | Publication: Not published | Owner: To assign
Purpose and boundary
Define the reusable COS framework, architecture ownership and relationships. Entity-specific configurations and actual transactions belong to the entity implementation.
Architecture model
Maintain the complete object hierarchy and relationships in Object_Register. Reconcile the platform, suite, engine, module and component hierarchy with entity domain and business-function ownership before freezing placements. No final object counts or new permanent ID prefixes are declared in this draft.
Design ownership
Use this document for architecture boundaries and object design references. Maintain suite and engine derivative specifications when warranted; module and component detail can remain within their owning design unless independent complexity or ownership requires a separate specification. This derivative strategy remains for review.
Document and register responsibilities
Architecture describes what exists and its relationships. Standards define how it is designed and maintained. Registers hold structured identities, decisions, changes, impacts, verification, releases and backups. Operational master and transaction datasets retain their own owners.
AI Chat and object design
Record AI Chat, AI Provider, AI Chat ID, AI Chat Link and optional AI Project name, ID and link. Scope and Entity determine ownership. Map one active primary design chat per object and preserve supporting and previous chats. A chat may propose cross-scope changes without becoming the approving authority.
Storage and consolidation
Proposed storage boundaries are Workspace for team interaction, System for governed configuration and owned datasets, and Raw for immutable source originals. Folder hierarchy need not reproduce every architecture level. Exact placement and migration mapping require review before moves.
Release architecture
Maintain two permanent files per logical artifact: _dft and _pub. Their file IDs remain stable. Apply approved content within the published file. Preserve latest operational Sheet data and existing tab IDs where possible. Publication must follow recorded approval and verification.
Open design questions
Resolve permanent ID prefixes, conflicting architecture inventories, exact folder locations, source-of-truth mappings, detailed formatting conflicts and backup retention. Existing sources remain in place until approved consolidation.
Next stage
Review the six drafts and governance registers. Approve the baseline and exact source-to-target mapping before consolidation or publication.


Governance file set and source review
This architecture draft works with COS_Standards_gov_dft and COS_Registers_gov_dft. The register contains decisions, change proposals, source-mapping review and backup references. Creating these drafts does not migrate operational data, replace existing authoritative sources or establish a published release.
Candidate sources include COS_Full_Export_v1.1.0.docx, COS_Global_Registers, reusable coding guidance and related engine/data-management designs. Reconcile conflicting hierarchy inventories and authority before adopting content.
Sources remain unchanged until replacement content, dependencies and references are verified and source-by-source consolidation is approved.


Identity and relational design update — 20-Oct-2026
D39 records the user direction to retain both UUIDs and readable prefixed IDs. The proposed implementation (D40) uses immutable UUID primary keys and UUID foreign keys, with readable IDs as unique alternate keys. Hierarchical codes support readability but do not replace explicit relationships. Existing SYS_EMP_ID and external provider identities remain traceable; no keys are allocated or migrated by this update.
Object ownership and cross-domain contracts
D41–D46 record proposed hierarchical codes, source/account-qualified identity mappings, configurable database enforcement, accountable table ownership and explicit Object_Table_Map roles. An object may own several tables or no direct operational table. Use mapping tables for many-to-many relationships. Shared identities connect domains; APIs/events carry approved contracts across services. Technical implementation and exact hierarchy patterns remain pending approval.
Development and project boundaries
D45 proposes top-down architecture and shared contracts followed by implementation of one dependency-complete component and workflow. D47 distinguishes architecture objects, delivery projects and deployments. D48 proposes COS_Governance, COS_Shared_Services and MHL_Payroll as candidates only; names and project count are not frozen. D49 records the user direction for one logical Project Name across Drive, Apps Script, AI and backend services, with platform IDs and environment/service distinctions maintained separately.
AI project and chat registration
D50 preserves one active primary design chat per object; progressive creation at suite, engine, module and component levels remains proposed. D51 records the user direction to preregister chat name and object, configure/create the AI project and chat, register actual provider IDs/links and verify before activation. D52–D53 propose separate internal/provider identities and project/platform mapping registers. Unavailable provider IDs remain blank.
Approval and implementation boundary
Decision_Register holds the detailed records and approval status; Change_Register links the proposed implementation. D57 proposes reconciling implemented database catalogue structure against approved design intent. D58 retains governance prefix proposals for review. No permanent prefixes, projects, chats, UUIDs or operational tables were created. Existing source consolidation remains pending source-by-source approval.

﻿COS_Standards_gov_dft
Draft governance baseline — version 0.1.0
Created 20-Oct-2026 | Publication: Not published | Owner: To assign
Purpose and authority
Working governance standard for COS. Version 0.1.0 is a draft baseline. Accepted-in-chat decisions are recorded separately from pending proposals; creation of this draft does not mark all controls approved or effective.
Naming
Use COS_Architecture_gov_dft, COS_Standards_gov_dft and COS_Registers_gov_dft. Corresponding published files use _pub. Keep STD_SYS and REG_SYS classifications out of these filenames. Maintain permanent IDs, short codes and display names in separate register fields.
Permanent draft and publication
Keep two permanent files per logical artifact. Edit drafts for proposed changes. At initial publication establish the permanent published ID. For later releases apply approved draft content within that published file; never replace it by renaming a new copy.
Backup policy
Use _bck consistently. Backup filename: <permanent filename>_bck_v<version>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>, with Asia/Kolkata timestamps. For an existing document, back up before each logical content update. Initial file creation is the first baseline and has no prior state to back up.
Sheet backup triggers
Back up before structural changes, material formula/rule/validation/mapping changes, bulk overwrites, deletions, merges, deduplication and reprocessing. At publication back up both draft and published files. Formatting-only edits normally require no full backup unless they rewrite data or structure.
Append and edit controls
Routine data appends need no full backup. Maintain unique record IDs, append timestamps and source/run references. Log routine existing-record edits with record ID, old/new values, actor and timestamp; log approval/status transitions. This draft defines requirements but installs no automation.
Operational Sheets
Use the draft for proposed structure, formulas and configuration. Approved operational appends may enter the published Sheet. Publication must preserve current live data; do not overwrite it from a stale draft. Assess dependencies before changing tab IDs, column names or formulas.
AI response and chat standard
Show ideas, suggestions and example tables in chat before generating or updating documents and Sheets, and obtain approval for the proposed work. Do not silently infer unresolved facts. Use AI Chat as the display field and preserve actual provider chat/project identifiers; leave unavailable IDs blank. Maintain one active primary design chat per object.
Decision and change control
Any chat can propose a decision. Record scope, reason, approval evidence, baseline and superseded decision references. Track each impacted target separately. Separate approval, implementation, verification and publication status. Do not rewrite historical transactions automatically when a standard changes.
Publishing procedure
Confirm approval and baseline, create required backups, apply the approved change inside the permanent published file, verify content and references, then record release outcome and effective version. On failure retain recovery references and mark publication failed; do not declare a release effective before verification.
Archive and history
Published backups preserve previous approved versions. A separate _arch copy is unnecessary for this workflow. Keep version, status, effective date and supersedes references internally. Backup retention and deletion policy remain unresolved.
Formatting and source adoption
Use readable headers, filters where useful, stable IDs separate from serial numbers, and full source links. Detailed inherited formatting rules and conflicts require reconciliation before a single formatting standard is frozen. Entity adoptions reference the approved COS version; local exceptions do not silently change the global standard.


AI Standard: selection and output controls
AI Standard is the umbrella; AI Chat Standard is a section. Before file generation or updates show content summary, relevant examples and the Selection form, then obtain explicit permission. Current authorisation covers completing six drafts only.
Show Content: Add Content (first and default), Summary, Full, Example, Suggestion, None. Show Dataset: Table Header, Test Dataset, Full Dataset, None. Both rows allow multiple choices; None clears other choices. Content Status: Draft/Approved, default Draft. Update File: Yes/No, default No. Generate New File: Yes/No, default No. Backup: Yes/No, default Yes when updating and disabled No for chat-only or initial creation. Mandatory backup policy takes precedence over a conflicting selection.
Show all rows together, with All files or individual file selection and adjacent related buttons. Retain per-file settings for different actions. For one target, Update File and Generate New File are mutually exclusive. Submit Selection previews the intended action; it does not itself authorise a write. Final content and approved content do not imply publication.
After submission show the selected register tabs' column headers or selected documents' section headings, and the requested dataset. Test Dataset means the latest 10 actual records, ordered by an identified relevant date/timestamp; show all if fewer than 10. If latest cannot be determined, ask which field to use. If live data is unavailable, state that limitation. Example means illustrative data and must be labelled separately.
Draft completion and approval boundary
The user authorised completion of the six fresh drafts. Source consolidation and publication remain pending. Backup, edit logging, uniqueness checks and publishing are control requirements; no runtime automation is installed by these drafts.


Global strict rule: shared-drive storage and local-file approval
Shared-drive-only storage applies across COS and MHL chats and projects. Use native Google Docs and Google Sheets under the approved shared-drive root https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KmWT6rD0EMBIDFIioE5KMShGB4Kb9u7y. Do not create or save deliverables in My Drive. Do not create local files, temporary local build/export files, Excel files or downloadable artifacts without explicit documented approval from ashish.maan@mannhospitality.com (main user/workspace authority). Do not treat a tool or skill default as approval. If the native shared-drive route cannot complete a task, stop before the prohibited operation and request that approval. Any user-specific local-file standard is maintained separately in that user's workspace and remains subject to this approval requirement. Current draft destination: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Ihxx88hRxupD41ve6aEw6OINY2mudHAi. Global applicability is a governance requirement; recording it does not automatically configure or enforce other chats or projects.
Instruction received: 20-Oct-2026. Status: User instruction, effective for current work. Draft document is not a published release. Exception approval must identify approver, scope, permitted file types/location and purpose.


Governance decision update — 20-Oct-2026
Decision references D39–D58 capture the latest discussion. User directions are recorded as approved directions; assistant proposals remain Pending. Updating these drafts does not approve every proposal, publish a baseline or authorise source consolidation.
Identifier and relational standards
D39: retain UUID and readable prefixed identity. D40–D43 and D58: proposed UUID keys, unique alternate readable IDs, explicit foreign keys, hierarchical short codes, controlled allocation, preservation of existing/external identities and configured database constraints. Exact prefixes, code order and allocations remain unresolved. No physical schema migration or permanent-ID issuance is performed.
Project and AI Chat standards
D49: use one registered logical Project Name across platforms where the project exists; preserve separate platform IDs and distinct environment/service names. D51: register planned chat name and object first, create/configure the project and chat, then record actual IDs/links and verify mapping before activation. D50 and D52–D53 retain proposals for progressive chat creation, internal/provider identity separation and supporting registers.
Backup and date clarification
D54: moving files without content/structural changes requires no backup. All backups belong in approved shared-drive 03_Backup: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1dQ_2t8ibU30HBx7x1gilqZA_JfRPbjpN. Back up documents before logical content updates; routine register appends remain exempt. D38/D55: user-readable date format is DD-MMM-YYYY, for example 20-Oct-2026. Time-of-day and filename collision conventions still require agreement. Existing filenames and historical values are not rewritten by this registration.
Scope, authority and next action
COS owns reusable definitions; MHL records entity application and adoption. Shared discussion references in the two draft registers represent scope-specific applicability, not independent permanent decision IDs. Final prefix and key registration follows approved schema review. These documents remain drafts; publication, runtime automation and source consolidation remain pending.

Uniqueness and matching
The requested composite key is Father Name + Nationality + National ID Type + ID Number. SYS_EMP_ID remains the canonical business identifier used in employee relationships. Apply the approved scope to both uniqueness constraints; the scope decision must be settled before a production migration.
Create the composite fingerprint using a keyed digest of a canonical, unambiguously encoded tuple. Use encryption for identifier recovery and a separate protected key reference for fingerprint generation. Do not use an ordinary unsalted hash of a low-entropy identifier. Version normalisation and fingerprint logic; key rotation requires a controlled dual-check/backfill transition.
A spelling change in father name could allow the same national ID under a different composite key. An additional same-nationality/type/ID duplicate-review check is proposed, not an approved replacement for the requested key. Identifier normalisation, issuer-country requirements and treatment of people without national ID remain pending business decisions.
Transactions and deletion
On execution, lock/claim the approved request; verify actor authority, config and identity constraints; allocate an Auto ID when needed; insert identity and responses; write request_result, audit and outbox; commit once. A unique constraint resolves simultaneous duplicate submissions. Do not allocate by MAX(id)+1. Sequence gaps may occur; gapless numbering is not promised.
Use RESTRICT for referenced master deletion; retire definitions or deactivate operational access through controlled requests. Do not cascade-delete employee history, approvals or audit. An actual erasure/retention policy requires separate approved handling.
